slides.title: Factorising monic quadratics
slides.lede: A monic quadratic is _x_^2 + _b__x_ + _c_ — the coefficient of _x_^2 is 1. Read the notes, watch the video, follow the worked examples, then complete the practice in your exercise book.

keyIdea.title: Key idea
keyIdea.body: Find two numbers that MULTIPLY to _c_ and ADD to _b_. Those two numbers go straight into the brackets, and expanding your answer checks it.

notes.body: Expanding turns (_x_ + 2)(_x_ + 3) into _x_^2 + 5_x_ + 6. Factorising turns it back. If your brackets expand to the original, you are right — so every answer can be checked without asking anyone.
A quadratic is monic when the coefficient of _x_^2 is 1: _x_^2 + _b__x_ + _c_. Today every expression is monic once any common factor is taken out.
Find two numbers whose product is _c_ and whose sum is _b_. For _x_^2 + 7_x_ + 12 that is 3 and 4, so the factors are (_x_ + 3)(_x_ + 4).

notes.term: Let the signs narrow the search
notes.body: If _c_ is positive, both numbers share the sign of _b_ — both positive, or both negative. If _c_ is negative, one is positive and one is negative, and the larger takes the sign of _b_.
2_x_^2 + 10_x_ + 12 is not monic — but take out the 2 and it becomes 2(_x_^2 + 5_x_ + 6), and the bracket is. Check for a common factor before anything else, and keep it in your answer.

video.note: Six minutes. Watch it once through, then again with a pen, pausing at each example.

workedExamples.title: The same method, three sign patterns
workedExamples.lede: Every one of these is multiply-to-_c_, add-to-_b_. Only the signs change.

steps.text: Check for a common factor first. There is none, and the coefficient of _x_^2 is 1, so the expression is monic.
The constant is positive and the middle term is positive, so both numbers are positive. You need two of them that multiply to 12 and add to 7.
There are only three factor pairs of 12 to try: 1 and 12 add to 13; 2 and 6 add to 8; 3 and 4 add to 7.
Put that pair into the brackets.
No common factor, and the expression is monic.
The constant is positive, so both numbers share a sign. The middle term is negative, so that shared sign is negative.
Two negatives that multiply to 6 and add to −5.
Put that pair into the brackets.
No common factor, and the expression is monic.
The constant is negative, so one number is positive and one is negative.
The pair is 5 and −3. The larger number takes the sign of the middle term, which is positive here.
Put that pair into the brackets.
Check by expanding — this is the step that makes the answer yours rather than the teacher’s.

workedExamples.title: When a common factor comes out first
workedExamples.lede: An expression that is not monic is often a monic one wearing a coat.

steps.text: Every term is divisible by 2. Take it out before anything else — and write it down, because it stays in the final answer.
The bracket is now monic. Two numbers that multiply to 6 and add to 5.
Factorise the bracket, keeping the 2 in front.
steps.note: Leaving out the 2 is the commonest mistake in this question type.
